title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is analysing an extension of group schemes over S_0 (in the 'Longue Marche' continuation, apparently around Teichmüller/braid-type groups; S may be Spec of Ẑ). Equation (243) is an extension of (𝔊_3)_{S_0} by a rank-2 lattice M = Zλ0 ⊕ Zλ1. M carries two automorphisms ρ_M and σ_M. On the previous page he parametrised 'scalings' (splittings) of (243) by pairs (ξ, η), with ξ in ΓM and η in an auxiliary rank-1 lattice spanned by δ. He wrote ξ = a0λ0 + a1λ1 and η = bδ, and showed that the splittings form the affine set Sc = {(a0, a1, b) : 2a1 − a0 − 3b = −1}, which is nonempty.

On this page:
(253) Sc is a torsor under Sc_0 = K, where K = ker(Z^3 → Z, (α0, α1, β) ↦ 2α1 − α0 − 3β). Since this map is surjective, K ≅ Z^2 (marginal note).

Next, M acts on Sc by conjugation: λ sends (ξ, η) to (λξρ(λ)^{-1}, λη                                                                                                σ(λ)^{-1}). Written additively this is (254): (ξ, η) ↦ (ξ + (1−ρ_M)λ, η + (1−σ_M)λ). This action factors through the torsor structure via the homomorphism (255): λ ↦ ((1−ρ)λ, (1−σ)λ). For λ = c0λ0 + c1λ1 one has (1−ρ)λ = (c0+c1)λ0 + (2c1−c0)λ1 and (1−σ)λ = (c1−c0)δ. In coordinates this is (256): M → K ⊂ Z^3, (c0, c1) ↦ (c0+c1, 2c1−c0, c1−c0).

In modern terms: splittings form a torsor under 1-cocycles Z^1. Conjugation by M acts through the coboundary map M → Z^1, λ ↦ (1−g)λ. Whether M → K is an isomorphism decides whether H^1 = 0 and M^G = 0, i.e. whether the scheme of splittings is an M-torsor. On the next page he concludes that it is: the map is universally injective, hence an isomorphism by rank. So all splittings are conjugate by a unique section of M, and the 'Proposition' states that the extension splits and its splittings form an M-torsor.
errors: No mathematical error. Check of (256): 2(2c1−c0) − (c0+c1) − 3(c1−c0) = 0, so the image lies in K.
In the coordinates (α1, β) on K, the map is (c0, c1) ↦ (−c0+2c1, −c0+c1). Its determinant is 1, so M → K is indeed an isomorphism, consistent with the Proposition on the next page.
The '1 → K' at the start of the exact sequence should be '0 → K', since these are additive Z-modules. This is a harmless notational slip.

ideas.what: The scheme of splittings of a group extension with abelian kernel is a torsor under the cocycles. Conjugation by the kernel acts through the coboundary map λ ↦ (1−g)λ. An isomorphism M ≅ Z^1 (so H^1 = 0 and M^G = 0) makes the splittings an M-torsor, with all splittings uniquely conjugate.
ideas.modern_name: Nonabelian/abelian H^1 classification of splittings; torsor of sections of an extension
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical group cohomology (Eilenberg–MacLane, Schreier); torsor language from Grothendieck/Giraud
ideas.where_published: SGA 3 (Exp. on extensions / H^1), Giraud 'Cohomologie non abélienne' in the same spirit

ideas.what: An explicit lattice computation showing the coboundary map M → K ≅ Z^2 is an isomorphism (determinant 1).
ideas.modern_name: Vanishing of H^1 of a finite (or virtually free) group acting on a rank-2 lattice

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine explicit cohomological computation (splittings = torsor under cocycles, coboundary map is an isomorphism) inside a longer analysis of some extension in the Longue Marche continuation. It is correct but standard and contains no new idea.
transcription_corrections: First line: likely 'torseur sous le schéma en groupes / sous un module' ('torseur sur les solutions un module' is garbled).
'par automorphismes [?]' is plausible; the handwriting suggests 'par automorphismes intérieurs' or similar.
'1 → K → Z^3 → Z → 0': the crossed-out text before Z^3 is a correction, and the superscript 3 is written above it.

On the next page, 'donc pas iso pour des questions de rang' should almost certainly read 'donc iso pour des questions de rang'. The determinant is 1 and the ensuing Proposition asserts an M-torsor structure.
On the previous page, 'Γ E^3' in (252) is most likely 'Γ Z^3' or 'ℤ^3'.
